title: Artificial Consistency Database Forced Migrations
pattern: Forcing the migration of a specialized, stable, and highly performant database (like a Redis cache or NoSQL store) to a relational database solely to enforce corporate architectural "uniformity."
why_bad: It overlooks specialized design trade-offs. Forcing a low-latency key-value cache into a relational database increases query complexity, ruins write performance, and introduces unnecessary locking, leading to system instability [108, 571].
detection: Migration proposals advocating the replacement of a data store without referencing any technical metrics (such as CPU, latency, or memory bottlenecks) or business-value gains [141, 586].
counterexample: Valid if the cost of supporting multiple database technologies outweighs the performance benefits and the target database easily meets the required SLAs. Mark as `Context-dependent`.
fix: Acknowledge cyclical and specialized data store patterns; prioritize technical requirements (low latency, high throughput) over artificial consistency [108, 571].
source: Kill It with Fire, Chapter 3, "Beware Artificial Consistency" [107, 108, 569, 570, 571, 586]
